commits.message: docs(evidence): record the owner ruling approving the §7.2 three-face superset (#633, #635)

Merge wave/decoding-72-closing-arm: the #633 §7.2 BindOutOfDomain closing arm

Step-03 gains the direction-B out-of-domain bind-time close (three
faces, disclosed strict superset of the decision text — owner ruling
requested in GOAL_PROGRESS), with the lib wire twin appended at tag 3,
8 selectors (family 85/85), two new exec-ledger rows + a third
neutralisation selector (verify pass, 23 rows), design-doc §3.2/§7.6
amendments, and the sweep-digest re-stamp after a green byte-identical
--check under the rebuilt blueprint (only the step-03 pair moves,
24,862 -> 25,767 B, 452 validators unchanged).

evidence(decoding,ledger): pin the closing arm's frontier face and repair the wave entry after review

Review findings applied: the exec ledger's out-of-domain row was not the
arm's worst case — the reference-field face measures 2,388,802 mem /
1,018,687,200 cpu against the pinned spend face's 2,382,579 /
1,016,343,454 — so closes_an_out_of_domain_reference_ordinal is now
pinned too (verify pass, 23 rows; both within the 13.2M basis). The
GOAL_PROGRESS entry gains the exact evidence commands, the blueprint
move (24,862 -> 25,767 B, 452 count unchanged), the sweep-check +
digest re-stamp record it omitted, and an explicit owner-ruling request
on the strict-superset faces: they convict on the committed reason's
encoding alone, and the machine-never-emits-them premise is asserted
from the machine's shape, not enforced by any range check on the
emitter.

Declined (recorded here): extracting a shared subject_field_view helper
and reordering the BindOutOfDomain when-clause to match tag order —
both were verified to move step-03's compiled bytes (clause order is
load-bearing for the compiled when-chain), and consensus-byte churn for
a legibility preference fails the tradeoff order. The tier-1-only
carriage coverage on the count face matches BindOutpoint's existing
precedent.

docs(fault-proofs,ledger): record the §7.2 closing arm in the design doc and GOAL_PROGRESS

Design doc: §3.2 gains the BindOutOfDomain arm (four Continue arms) with
the strict-superset reasoning spelled out; §7.6 gains the out-of-domain
accusation-subjects edge case, including the one-way soundness argument
and the pinned neutralisation selector. GOAL_PROGRESS records the wave
(branch wave/decoding-72-closing-arm off checkpoint 0e248f41), the
strict-superset disclosure, the exec-ledger movements, and the vacuous
aiken -m filter finding.

feat(onchain/decoding): add the #633 §7.2 BindOutOfDomain closing arm to step-03

Executes the offchain plan's §7.2 decision (delegated 2026-08-25): a
forced leaf whose verbatim accusation pair names a subject BindOutpoint
can only abort on (§7.3 abort-never-clamp) is no longer unprovable —
direction B closes it at bind with the class-0 contradiction marker on
the still-unbound state, which step-04's direction-B gate consumes
unchanged. The wire twin appends BindOutOfDomain LAST, so the
BindOutpoint/Scan/Verdict redeemer tags are unmoved.

Strict-superset disclosure: the decision text names one face
(outpoint_cursor >= |field|, proven via the §8.8 door's authenticated
item count). The landed arm closes three — that face, a negative
ordinal, and source_kind outside {0, 1} — because the rejection-reason
arms carry source_kind as an unvalidated Int and step-02's ruled
verbatim copy forwards it, making the extra faces the same unprovable
corner and the same fault statement (the accusation names a subject the
machine could never have resolved). The two extra faces close with no
field opening; the canonical redeemer carries None there. Soundness runs
one way: the machine only emits in-domain pairs, so the arm can never
close against an honest operator's leaf. Step-02's verbatim copy stays
unguarded by design and now says so.

Selectors: 4 positive (spend-field count face, reference-field count
face, negative ordinal, source_kind naming no field) and 4 refusals
(in-domain ordinal, direction A, post-bind re-close, non-canonical
opening on the negative face). Family suite 85/85 under the fork
(v1.1.23+6801f62).

Exec ledger: new step_03 row closes_an_out_of_domain_ordinal (2,382,579
mem / 1,016,343,454 cpu, within the 13.2M basis) and a third
neutralisation selector (rejects_an_in_domain_ordinal_close — were the
count comparison neutralised, a prover could convict an operator whose
correct in-domain rejection was never disproven). The five pre-existing
step_03 rows moved by the new arm's dispatch cost (+0.6-1.5K mem) and
are re-pinned here per the ledger's move-in-the-same-commit rule;
verify green, 22 rows.

Blueprint: only the step-03 spend/else pair moves (24,862 -> 25,767 B
compiled; still over the 16,384 inline envelope, so the plan's Q3
reference-scripts answer stands); 452 validators unchanged. Resolver
sweep --check byte-identical under the rebuilt blueprint (the decoding
validators are unregistered), so the inputs digest is re-stamped after
that green check per the sanctioned flow.

Also found: 'aiken check -m native_script_decoding' matches ZERO tests
(a bare -m string is a test-name filter; module filters need a '/' or
'.{..}') — prior green runs under that filter were vacuous. Working
filters: -m 'native_script_decoding/' or -m decoding_step_03.

Merge fix/642-fail-surface: the #642 fail-surface wave

All five findings of consolidated issue #642 implemented: zz605 doc-
comment trip reworded (never allowlisted), complete-item-proof-fit
re-pinned onto #640 with measured dual-blueprint attribution, the native
architecture-g-owner built in node global-setup (throw on compile
regression, loud skip only without cargo), min-Ada-compliant fixtures for
the two phase-B parallelization tests, the resolver proof-fit sweep
re-pinned with the first inputs-digest stamp, and the scan bench
restructured to subprocess-per-measurement around the uplc wasm ceiling.
The scan-ledger bootstrap itself remains owner-gated and is not
performed. Full three-lane suite at the branch tip: only the
pre-existing expected reds (watcher 15, fault-proofs 1, sdk 1, node 3).

test(node,fault-proofs): close the #642 review findings

- global-setup: a native architecture-g-owner build failure with cargo
  AVAILABLE now throws — that is a compile regression in the crate, and
  degrading seven real assertions into skips would hide it. Only a
  genuinely missing toolchain (no cargo, or MIDGARD_SKIP_NATIVE_BUILD=1)
  keeps the loud-skip path. The build goes through the package script
  (native:mpf-owner:build) so the argv lives in one place.
- tests/helpers/native-owner-binary.ts: single owner of the binary path,
  presence probe, and skip warning; global-setup and both mpf consumer
  files now share it instead of carrying three copies.
- validation-parallelization: the PHASE_B_COMPLIANT_LOVELACE comment now
  says why 5M rather than the 849,070 floor (headroom — these tests are
  about conflicts/intervals, not the floor's boundary).
- zz605: the allowlist comment records that the gate matches FILE TEXT,
  comments included — a prose compiledCode mention trips it exactly like
  a real read, deliberately; reword doc comments, never allowlist.

mpf-differential 1/1, mpf-native-owner-service 6/6,
validation-parallelization 7/7, zz605 8/8; node typecheck clean; eslint
clean on every touched file.

evidence(validation): isolate scan-bench measurements per process (#642 item 5)

The single-process ExUnits benchmark cannot complete a full curve:
@lucid-evolution/uplc leaks wasm linear memory per evaluation, wasm32
never shrinks, and the run traps with an opaque 'unreachable' at exactly
deep-65 native:finalize — reproduced identically before and after the
applyParamsToScript memoization, so the leak is the measured evaluations
themselves and only a process boundary isolates it (vitest isolates per
FILE, not per test).

scripts/run-scan-bench-evidence-v1.mjs orchestrates the benchmark file
through three env modes it now understands:
  list    — resolve curve points (incl. maxfit) + selected step labels
  measure — one fresh process per (shape, nodes, label): one evaluation
            on a fresh wasm heap; positivity asserted, ledger NOT judged
            (a narrowed child judging is the truncated-pin shape
            checkScanBenchLedgerV1 exists to refuse)
  check   — judge the orchestrator-merged readings against the committed
            ledger, with the CALLER's own filter env restored verbatim so
            the truncated-bootstrap refusal still sees it; UPDATE reaches
            this child only.
Point-level fields must agree across a point's children (build
determinism) or the merge refuses loudly; any child failure aborts before
judgement. test:evidence(:update) now front the bench with the
orchestrator.

Verified: deep-5 narrowed run — 10/10 measure children green in fresh
processes, merge consistent, check child red with exactly the honest
'no committed artifact' structural failure (the bootstrap stays with the
owner), orchestrator exit mirroring it. Package typecheck clean.

evidence(validation): re-pin the resolver proof-fit sweep onto #640 and establish the first inputs-digest stamp (#642)

The 'not byte-identical' regen red was not nondeterminism: two independent
regenerations produced byte-identical artifacts, both differing from the
committed fixture in exactly eight scriptHash lines — the #640
da-hash-preimage moved-hash class (28db415e... among them, the same move
item 2 re-pinned). No ExUnits, byte, or fit field moved. The fixture is the
regenerated artifact; the sanctioned flow then went green end-to-end:
generate --check byte-identical, digest --stamp, gate PASS, sweep file 4/4.

This is the digest gate's FIRST stamp ('currency has never been established'
was the default lane's honest red). The declared closure includes the
gitignored onchain/aiken/plutus.json, so the stamp binds the blueprint built
from THIS tree's onchain source (452 validators, md5
78540c1d34b10d205942372882487a00, aiken v1.1.23+6801f62) — the gate reads
current only where that exact blueprint is staged, which is the closure's
deliberate fail-closed design.

fix(node): min-Ada-compliant fixtures for the two phase-B parallelization tests (#642)

Root cause found by probing the rejection codes: both reds were E_MIN_ADA
(output[0] 10 < 849,070 for 37 serialized bytes) — the fixtures' 10-lovelace
outputs predate the #618 min-Ada floor (R8 of decision 0005), so every
candidate was rejected before conflict detection or interval evaluation was
reached. Raising the fixture amounts to 5,000,000 lovelace restores the
behaviours under test: bucket conflict resolution (A accepted, B double-spend
rejected, C accepted) and both validity-interval polarities, including the
exact '120 > 119' rejection detail. The failures were fully deterministic and
in-memory — the earlier database-state correlation was a misattribution.
File 7/7.

fix(node): build the native architecture-g-owner in global-setup; loud skip when absent (#642)

The dedicated scripts (test:mpf:differential, test:mpf-native-owner) always
built the binary, but the plain test run never did, so a fresh worktree failed
mpf-differential and mpf-native-owner-service on a missing artifact. Global
setup now runs cargo build --release --locked (sub-second when warm,
MIDGARD_SKIP_NATIVE_BUILD=1 opts out, missing cargo degrades gracefully), and
both consumer files skip LOUDLY — console warning naming the path and the
build command — when the binary is still absent. Never a silent pass: the
skip is visible per-file in the vitest summary. Both polarities verified:
7/7 pass with the binary; 7 loud skips without it.

fix(validation): re-pin the §3.2 necessity identities onto the #640 deployment (#642)

The #640 merge's da-hash-preimage/rule.ak fix recompiled the fraud-proof
validators that fold that rule, moving resolver[1]'s applied hash
81b42c84... -> 28db415e.... Measured through loadContracts() — the same
producer the row asserts on — under both the base 0df64631 blueprint (444
validators) and the current tree's (452): identical triples, so the move is
entirely #640's and the #635 wave's appended validators touch none of the
identities. COUNT (91) and the proof-item hash are unchanged. File 6/6.

fix(fault-proofs): reword a doc comment that tripped the zz605 compiledCode allowlist gate (#642)

165db5ca's ValueAndMint deployment-size comment in validation-dispute/submit.ts
mentioned the literal token the zz605 scan confines to allowlisted loaders.
The file performs no bare read — rewording the comment keeps the gate precise
instead of allowlisting a comment-only file, which would mask any future real
bare read added there. zz605 back to 8/8.
